method_note: Reviewer-proposed directional codings, not issued Humanity Scores. Sources are public primary-party documentation. No signed snapshot or signed human review is represented.
correction_rule: Evidence- or methodology-based corrections only; payment cannot buy a higher score or favorable conclusion.

findings.finding: Letta Code exposes standard, strict, acceptEdits and unrestricted execution permission modes.
findings.limitation: Company-authored documentation establishes what is documented, not independently observed real-world performance.

findings.finding: In strict mode Letta Code requires a prompt before every tool call, while standard mode asks before approval-requiring actions.
findings.limitation: The interactive CLI is documented to start in unrestricted mode by default; users must choose stricter controls.

findings.finding: Letta Code interactive CLI defaults to unrestricted permission mode, which automatically permits tool calls unless blocked by safeguards.
findings.limitation: This documented default is a concern for unintended actions; actual deployment-specific configuration is unknown.

findings.finding: Letta's desktop app lets a user view and directly edit an agent's memory, skills, channels and schedules.
findings.limitation: Editable state is not evidence that all executed downstream actions can be undone.

findings.finding: Letta's desktop app surfaces sent and received channel messages, schedule run history and editable memory files.
findings.limitation: Company-authored documentation establishes what is documented, not independently observed real-world performance.

findings.finding: Letta documents a free entry plan using BYOK and a usage-based API path for developer applications.
findings.limitation: Company-authored documentation establishes what is documented, not independently observed real-world performance.

findings.finding: Letta's privacy policy says data sent to Letta-hosted services, including messages and responses, may be used for service improvement including future model training.
findings.limitation: Policy states permitted use; does not prove any particular user's data was trained on.

findings.finding: The same Letta privacy policy distinguishes self-hosted model backends and says message/prompt data is not collected by Letta outside its hosted services.
findings.limitation: This is limited to the deployment patterns specified by Letta.

findings.finding: Letta documents an open-source agent runtime, self-hosting, and model-provider choice.
findings.limitation: Model or deployment portability is not identical to zero switching cost.

findings.finding: Letta publishes plan limits and prices including free BYOK, $20/month personal Pro, $20/month API plus usage charges, and $20/seat/month Teams Pro.
findings.limitation: Prices may change; usage charges can increase total cost.

findings.finding: Letta team permissions document organization roles and selective sharing of agents, with conversations private to their creator by default.
findings.limitation: Company-authored documentation establishes what is documented, not independently observed real-world performance.

findings.finding: Letta documents proactive schedules, recurring tasks and autonomous agent execution while allowing users to set controls; the net effect on human work is not demonstrated.
findings.limitation: Real-world substitution and displacement cannot be inferred from feature documentation.

findings.finding: Letta provides a free BYOK route and publishes interfaces for local apps and command-line operation.
findings.limitation: BYOK may still incur third-party model costs and CLI use requires technical skill.
